text: Godel's Completeness Theorem asserts that $T \models \sigma$ if and only if $T \vdash \sigma$ (semantic entailment coincides with syntactic provability).
explanation: The Completeness Theorem equates semantics ($\models$, true in all models of $T$) with syntax ($\vdash$, formally derivable), and it is what makes the Compactness Theorem follow. It must not be confused with the Incompleteness theorems, which concern true-but-unprovable sentences within a single fixed theory.
